t: This is Lloyd's of London, in the City. It isn't an insurance company at all, but a market, where backers grouped in syndicates come together to pool and spread risk. Those backers include corporations and private individuals, traditionally called Names. The name comes from Edward Lloyd, who owned a London coffee house. He is the origin of the Lloyd's market, and also of Lloyd's List, the shipping journal, and Lloyd's Register. So a coffee house owner's name now sits over a whole institution.
